items.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Dillahunty directly separates occasional cognitive error from global unreliability and identifies replication prediction investigation and independent confirmation as practical mechanisms for discovering mistakes. Principal limitation: Success in perceptual and scientific correction does not automatically prove equal reliability in morally contested domains where values measurements and causal consequences can remain difficult to isolate. Live burden: He must connect these correction methods specifically to moral inquiry and specify how public evidence adjudicates conflicts involving incommensurable interests rather than merely factual disagreement.

items.currentText: Demonstrated that conflicting revelations do not automatically resolve moral disagreement.
items.lockedProposition: First-person revelation neither resolves conflicting divine claims nor fixes the disagreement and motivation problems raised against secular morality.

items.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Dillahunty tests revelation against actual disagreement by noting that equally convinced claimants can report incompatible divine messages without a shared procedure capable of resolving their conflict. Principal limitation: Denominational diversity illustrates the difficulty but does not prove that every revelation claim lacks evidence or that theological adjudication can never use historical textual and experiential criteria. Live burden: He must compare the reliability of revelation and public inquiry under equivalent standards while distinguishing unresolved disagreement from proof that no claimant possesses truth.
